summary: HfO2 thin films were deposited using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) with HfCp(NMe2)3 as the precursor and O2 plasma as the oxidizing agent. The process was carried out over a temperature range of 150–400 /C14 C, resulting in a growth per cycle of approximately 1.1 A˚ /cycle. The films showed reduced impurity levels and improved stoichiometry with increasing temperature, transitioning from amorphous to polycrystalline phases at 400 /C14 C. The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of this PEALD process for producing high-quality HfO2 films suitable for various applications.
evidence: HfO2 thin films were prepared by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition using a cyclopentadienylalkylamido precursor [HfCp(NMe2)3] and O2 plasma over a temperature range of 150–400 /C14 C at a growth per cycle around 1.1 A˚ /cycle.
